t.E163.agn: In 2013 EFSA did not set a numerical ADI because data were insufficient; it reported that aqueous extracts of edible fruits and vegetables are unlikely to raise concern at current uses.
t.E163.body: Anthocyanins are poorly absorbed from the digestive tract; the urine of people who eat foods containing anthocyanins is not coloured.
t.E163.prod: Obtained by extraction from fruits and vegetables.
t.E163.regx.0: No numerical ADI; concern unlikely for fruit and vegetable extracts.
t.E163.summary: Red, purple and blue pigments in fruits and vegetables such as grape skins, purple carrots and blackberries. Used in drinks, jams and confectionery.
t.E163.what: Gives a red, purple or blue colour. Anthocyanins also occur naturally in fruits and vegetables.
